newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive's sale of ABB surprises market.
newsitem.headline: Incentive's sale of ABB surprises market.

text.p: Swedish investment and medical technology group Incentive surprised the market on Wednesday by announcing it was selling half of its stake in Sweden's ABB AB for 12.4 billion crowns ($1.6 billion).
While market players had expected Incentive to continue its restructuring to concentrate on its medical technology unit Gambro, they were surprised by the timing and structure of the deal.
Incentive said it had sold 6.5 billion crowns worth of the shares to Swedish investment group Investor.
Both companies are part of the extensive industrial empire run by Sweden's powerful Wallenberg family. Investor is the family's key investment vehicle.
"It is another one of those Wallenberg shake-ups," said one broker.

Incentive said the sale was part of a rapid divestment process enabling it to focus on Gambro, which this week completed its tender offer for Vivra, the second largest dialysis provider in the United States.

"We can now fully integrate Vivra into our (medical technology unit) Gambro AB, thereby strengthening our leading global position in renal care and renal products," Incentive's chief exective Mikael Lilius said.
Incentive said it had sold the other 6.0 billion crown worth of shares to Morgan Stanley Dean Witter for sale to institutional investors.
The divestment was the latest in a string of sales by Incentive in the past few years.
The company has already disposed of its holdings in Hasselblad, Garphyttan car components unit, trading company AKA, and electricity company SEV to focus on its business area of medical technology.
The announcement came after the Stockholm bourse had closed for the day,
